subject: Tailored reservation fit questionnaire / EdgeScale RFP
messages:
From: Tanya Lopez <tanya.lopez@edgescale.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@edgescale.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: Dedicated inference reservation questionnaire

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for taking our call last week. We're kicking off the procurement track for a dedicated inference contract and attached our RFP pack (ES_RFP_Details.pdf). The security and licensing sections look fine; procurement asked us to confirm dedicated capacity sizing assumptions so we can model budget and run internal approvals.

Key asks from our side:
- A recommended GPU mix (family + count) to meet a long‑tail 95th percentile token throughput of ~18M tokens/min with a peak burst to 45M tokens/min for short windows.
- Guidance on how Redwood autoscaling/burst lanes would apply to that profile and how billed usage versus committed capacity is reconciled.
- Any constraints on model families for autoscale/fallback (e.g., if a quantized variant is used as fallback).
- A sample cost workbook to slot into our procurement model.

Can your team complete the attached questionnaire and return a proposed sizing worksheet by EOD Wednesday? We're on a tight internal calendar.

Thanks,
Tanya
Procurement Manager
EdgeScale

--
Attachment: ES_RFP_Details.pdf (application/pdf, 1.2MB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tanya Lopez <tanya.lopez@edgescale.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated inference reservation questionnaire

Tanya —

Appreciate the RFP packet. Attached is a starter workbook (redwood-dedicated-pricing-workbook.xlsx) that maps GPU families to throughput assumptions and cost curves. High level responses below; I'll follow up with a more granular slotting workbook once you confirm the workload mix.

Summary answers:
- Recommended starting mix: a weighted blend of A100-80GB for steady-state model variants (60%) + H100-80GB for peak short bursts (40%). For heavy quantized LLMs where latency is crucial, we suggest an M-series (M60x) quantized profile for cost‑sensitive background jobs.
- For your profile (18M tkn/min 95th, 45M burst), we estimate committed pool capacity ~10 A100-equivalent GPUs with autoscale/burst capacity to cover peak windows (auto-burst policy enabled for up to 3x committed for short durations). Exact slotting depends on session length and mean sequence length.
- Billing reconciliation: committed capacity is invoiced monthly; burst beyond committed is billed pay-as-you-go at a premium rate. We can cap total burst spend via policy if procurement needs hard limits.
- Fallback constraints: fallback to quantized variants is supported for most model families we host; however, for customers requiring exact determinism we recommend pinning model versions or disabling quantized fallback.

Next steps I need from you:
1) a small sample of your request trace (CSV) with distribution by sequence length and token counts (for the solver to pack batches efficiently), and
2) confirmation of the target SLOs (p50/p95 latency goals) for the traffic above.

If you can share the traffic profile, Ben and I can produce a tailored reservation worksheet by Wednesday EOD.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood-dedicated-pricing-workbook.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Oliver Zhang <oliver.zhang@edgescale.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tanya Lopez <tanya.lopez@edgescale.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated inference reservation questionnaire

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick reply. Attached is a slice of our production trace (EdgeScale_traffic_profile.csv). A few clarifications:
- The 18M tkn/min 95th assumes average seq length ~= 64 tokens; p95 sessions are mostly chat-style (shorter sequences) while p50 includes longer batch jobs (seq lengths up to ~512).
- Latency SLO: p50 target 120ms, p95 target 400ms (token-latency measured per token for streaming replies).
- We expect ~300 concurrent sessions during the p95 windows, spiking to ~750 during marketing events (these bursts typically last 3–8 minutes).

Also, procurement asked whether Redwood supports an initial pilot (90 days) with a smaller committed pool and predictable conversion path to full reservation — ideally with a one‑time credit if we convert early. Is that something you can include in your proposal?

-Oliver

--
Attachment: EdgeScale_traffic_profile.csv (text/csv, 120KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Zhang <oliver.zhang@edgescale.com>, Tanya Lopez <tanya.lopez@edgescale.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2027 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated inference reservation questionnaire

Oliver / Tanya —

Thanks for the profile — that was very helpful. We've run the profile through our packing solver and attached a concrete reservation proposal (es-reservation-proposal-v1.xlsx). Key highlights and assumptions:

- Proposed committed pool: 8 A100-80GB + 4 H100-80GB (equivalent to ~12.5 A100-equivalents for mixed workloads)
  - Rationale: this sizing meets your steady 95th throughput with room for rapid scaling; A100s handle the majority of steady chat traffic economically, H100s cover high-memory/throughput tails and expedite quantized fallback transitions.
- Autoscale/burst: policy configured to allow up to 3x committed for bursts up to 10 minutes, with burst spend billed at +45% over committed unit price. We modelled expected burst minutes from your CSV; expected monthly burst bill under the proposed cap is ~18% of committed spend.
- Latency: with the proposed mix and continuous KV caching for recurrent prefixes, we project p50 = ~95–120ms and p95 = ~320–380ms for your traffic distribution (detailed per-path latencies in the workbook).
- Pilot option: we can do a 90-day pilot at 40% committed scaling (3 A100 + 2 H100) with explicit conversion credit equal to 25% of pilot fees applied to first 6 months of full reservation if you convert within 90 days. We include that in the workbook under commercial terms.
- Model fallback: quantized variants will be used for non‑deterministic tasks; for any endpoints requiring exact model parity we recommend pinning. We included a compatibility matrix for common families in the attachment.

Open items before we finalize:
- Confirm whether marketing-event bursts need a higher hard cap (we can add an opt-in extra burst band that only triggers during calendar-defined events).
- Confirm whether you'd like us to reserve a small pool for on-call preemption tolerance (recommended for HA during bursts).

I'll schedule a short walkthrough of the workbook tomorrow if that helps — Ben will join to cover cost modeling.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: es-reservation-proposal-v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
